title: Quasi-separatedness from a quasi-compact relation projection
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Point spaces carry the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. An algebraic space is quasi-compact if its point space is quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover); it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback along every affine scheme mapping to its target has quasi-compact point space; it is quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $X$ be an algebraic space and let $q:U\to X$ be a representable surjective etale map from a scheme $U$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose $U$ is quasi-separated as a scheme [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] and one of the projections $U\times_XU\to U$ is quasi-compact. Then $X$ is quasi-separated. No quasi-compactness of $U$ or $X$ and no finite-presentation hypothesis over $S$ is required.

proof.text: First reconcile the quasi-compactness conventions. For any algebraic space $C$, quasi-compactness of $|C|$ gives a surjective etale affine atlas by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]; its source is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Conversely a quasi-compact scheme atlas gives a quasi-compact point space by [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas]. For a morphism $f:A\to B$ satisfying the affine-scheme-test condition in the statement and any quasi-compact space $C\to B$, choose such an affine atlas $V\to C$. Then $|A\times_BV|$ is quasi-compact by the hypothesis. The map $A\times_BV\to A\times_BC$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and its point map is continuous and surjective by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Pulling back an open cover to this quasi-compact source and taking a finite subcover proves $|A\times_BC|$ quasi-compact; the first observation gives a quasi-compact scheme atlas. Conversely the all-quasi-compact-space test implies the affine test since an affine scheme has a quasi-compact identity atlas. Thus the affine-scheme-test condition agrees with the all-quasi-compact-space convention in [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local].

source.place: Tags 03H6 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover), 03E4 (lemma-quasi-compact-space); spaces-descent.tex Tag 041L: convention comparison for its application

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] to $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. It gives the same scheme atlas $q:U\to X$ after viewing $X$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, and preserves the relation $R=U\times_XU$ with its two projections. The point representatives and topology agree because the atlas is unchanged. The assumptions on $U$ and on the selected relation projection are therefore unchanged. Work henceforth over $Z=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and write products over $Z$ explicitly. We are proving quasi-compactness of the absolute diagonal, not merely the diagonal over $S$.

source.place: Tag 07S4, proof first sentence; spaces.tex Tag 03I4 (lemma-change-base-scheme)

proof.text: Put $P=U\times_ZU$, $Y=X\times_ZX$, $a=q\times q:P\to Y$, and $j=(p_1,p_2):R\to P$. The map $a$ factors as $U\times_ZU\to X\times_ZU\to X\times_ZX$; each factor is a base change of $q$. By [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], $a$ is representable surjective etale. The space $R$ is a scheme because it is a scheme base change of the representable $q$; $P$ is a scheme fibre product. The square with top $R\to X$, bottom $a:P\to Y$, and right $\Delta_X:X\to Y$ is cartesian: on any test scheme a point of its pullback is $(u_1,u_2,x)$ with $q(u_1)=x=q(u_2)$, equivalently $(u_1,u_2)\in U\times_XU$. Forgetting $x$ and inserting $q(u_1)$ are inverse and natural. Under this identification the left map is $j$ and $\operatorname{pr}_i\circ j=p_i$ for both $i$.

Choose the index $i\in\{1,2\}$ for which $p_i:R\to U$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis. The scheme projection $\pi_i:P\to U$ is the base change of $U\to Z$ along $U\to Z$. Since $U$ is quasi-separated, this structure map is quasi-separated by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. The base-change clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes $\pi_i$ quasi-separated. This uses no quasi-compactness of $U$.

Apply [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target] to the triangle of schemes $R\xrightarrow{j}P\xrightarrow{\pi_i}U$. Its composite is the quasi-compact $p_i$, and its second arrow is quasi-separated by the preceding step. Its main assertion gives that $j$ is quasi-compact. The lemma does not require that its first arrow be an open immersion; only its final additional clause mentions that case. Here the assumed affine-scheme tests for $p_i$ in particular include affine open subschemes of $U$, so $p_i$ is quasi-compact as a scheme morphism. Conversely the scheme quasi-compactness just proved for $j$ implies the affine-scheme-test condition: for any affine $T\to P$, [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change] makes $R\times_PT\to T$ quasi-compact; since $T$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes $R\times_PT$ quasi-compact.

Use [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local] for $\Delta_X:X\to Y$ and the singleton covering $\{a:P\to Y\}$. Its base change is $j$ by step 3, hence quasi-compact. Its covering hypotheses hold: $a$ is representable surjective etale; scheme tests are etale and therefore flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. These are also the chartwise properties, since compositions with etale charts remain etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Surjectivity on field-valued point classes follows from [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. The conventions agree by step 1, so the descent conclusion says exactly that $\Delta_X$ is quasi-compact with the affine-scheme-test definition above. By its definition of absolute quasi-separatedness, $X$ is quasi-separated. The choice of $i$ covers either projection, and no step used finite presentation over $S$ or quasi-compactness of $X$ or $U$.

The statement matches Stacks 07S4 (spaces-properties.tex:822-845) hypothesis by hypothesis, with quasi-separated meaning the absolute diagonal over Spec Z. Step 1 shows the affine-test and all-quasi-compact-space conventions agree, using qc-space-affine-etale-atlas, affine-scheme-qcqs, the 'In particular' clause of a1-finite-affine-subatlas, fibre-products-etale-covers and a1-point-open-calculus. Step 2 changes the base to Z via change-base-to-integers (1) and (3). Step 3 builds the cartesian square with a=q×q as two base changes (representable-etale-scheme-tests). Step 4 gets a quasi-separated projection by base change (qcqs-permanence (3)). Step 5 gets j quasi-compact from the QuasiCompact.of_comp leaf; it implicitly identifies |h_T| with T for a scheme, which is elementary from def-a1-space-point-topology (advisory only). Step 6 descends along the singleton étale cover with sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local (041L) in place of Stacks' appeal to 02WZ; this is valid and stays in the unit. proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses, there is no cycle, and there is no SGA reference. Edge cases tested: U empty, identity atlas on a non-quasi-compact quasi-separated U, an arbitrary non-quasi-separated base S, and either projection. I accept the four declared tool_uses (lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas, lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers, lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests) as generic algebraic-space foundations.
